answer: Registration binds each identity to a one-per-hardware credential, the pearl, plus proof-of-work that must be redone for every new key. Faking an identity therefore costs a fresh proof plus a bond locked for 30 epochs and a 50 percent slash on detection. Splitting gains nothing, since marginal cost per fake stays flat, the shared bond slashes once, and independent sparrow jurors flag the spiral of duplicate proofs.
